title: Hierarchical Priors in Perceptual Uncertainty and Psychosis Proneness - A Random-Dot Kinematogram task with low- and high-level priors
description: EEG-BIDS dataset of cue-locked EEG recordings and event annotations from 43 neurotypical adults performing a random-dot kinematogram motion discrimination task. The task dissociates low-level priors (implicitly learned tone-motion contingencies) from high-level priors (a cover story about tinted glasses) against a neutral baseline. The data support analyses of hierarchical priors with signal detection theory, drift-diffusion modeling, and occipital oscillatory and aperiodic EEG activity, alongside psychosis-proneness and psychological flexibility questionnaires.
methods_description: Continuous EEG was recorded at 1000 Hz from 31 active Ag/AgCl electrodes (10/20 system, actiChamp Plus; ground FPz, online reference FCz). Participants completed a within-subject RDK left/right motion discrimination task with baseline, low-level prior and high-level prior conditions. Motion coherence was individualized with two QUEST staircases targeting 75% accuracy. Stimuli were presented with PsychoPy on a 240 Hz monitor at 65 cm viewing distance. Post-experimental questionnaires assessed manipulation checks, belief strength, psychosis proneness and psychological flexibility.
